content: An early 11th/17th-century account (Kāzirūnī, Sullam al-Samāvāt) has Ibn Turka and Sharaf al-Dīn sojourning in Baghdad in search of a Sufi master to discipline themselves to. Melvin-Koushki says it should be taken with several grains of salt, while noting that Kāzirūnī's source was likely his teacher Afżal al-Dīn b. Ḥabīb Allāh Turka (d. 991/1583).
